title: The supper of the Lamb (Apocalypse 19:6–9)
hookLine: blessed are they that are called: echoed at every Mass

lines: THERE'S GOING TO BE A WEDDING.
cards: Alleluia is sung at Mass all year, except in Lent. It's in hymns, on Easter cards, in the names of choirs. Now look for it in the Apocalypse: in chapter nineteen it comes four times, close together.

Right after Babylon falls, the noise of the merchants weeping is drowned out by another sound. John hears what sounds like a great crowd, like many waters, like great thunders, shouting alleluia. Then they say why.
There's going to be a wedding.

teach.b: The crowd sings that the Lord God Almighty reigns. Let us be glad and rejoice, they say, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.
She's given fine linen to wear, bright and clean, and the text explains the linen: it's the good deeds of the saints. So the bride is the Church, God's people, dressed in the love they've lived.
Babylon was dressed in purple and scarlet, bought and sold.
The bride is dressed in deeds.

teach.h: WRITE IT DOWN: BLESSED ARE THEY.
teach.b: Then an angel tells John to write something down, in the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb." These are the true words of God, the angel adds.

Again and again in the Bible, God's love for his people is pictured as a marriage, from the prophets to Jesus's parable of the wedding feast. Here that picture becomes a feast. Catholics hear it at every Mass.

teach.h: BEHOLD THE LAMB, AT EVERY MASS.
teach.b: Just before Communion, the priest holds up the host and says, behold the Lamb of God, and then that those called to the supper of the Lamb are blessed. In Latin: beati qui ad cenam Agni vocati sunt.

teach.h: BLESSED ARE THEY THAT ARE CALLED.
teach.b: The people answer with the words of a centurion from Matthew's Gospel, as the Douay-Rheims gives them: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word.
Called, and not worthy, and coming anyway. The Church teaches that every Mass is a foretaste of this wedding feast.

how: Before Communion at every Mass, the priest shows the host and says Behold the Lamb of God, adding that those called to the supper of the Lamb are blessed; the people respond with the centurion's words, Lord, I am not worthy, and the Church teaches that the Eucharist anticipates the wedding feast of the Lamb.

the merchants weep; the crowd shouts alleluia and announces a wedding.
in Apocalypse 19 the bride's fine linen stands for the saints' good deeds
the bride, God's people, is dressed in the love they've lived.

games.q: you're at Mass. the priest holds up the host: behold the Lamb of God, blessed are those called to his supper. you know you're not worthy. what do the people say?
o: the centurion's words: Lord, I am not worthy, but only say the word.
games.why: the people answer with the centurion's words from Matthew 8: not worthy, and coming anyway, because they're called.

practice: Picture the moment at Mass just before Communion: the host lifted, the quiet in the church, the words behold the Lamb of God, and then the line about those called to the supper.
Hear it as an invitation with your name on it, to a wedding feast already being set, and notice what comes up.
If you pray, answer in the centurion's words, Lord, I am not worthy, but only say the word; if not, just sit with being invited.
